strongest_case: The strongest defensible case is that FeltCraft-Lifetimes targets an important paper-level question with an unusually disciplined causal-credit boundary: immutable public experience is the only evidence source; DREAM proposes but cannot certify; later ordinary outcomes ground; SLEEP only transforms admitted content; text, graph, and LoRA are separated from reader--THINK composition; common-deck evaluation is separated from on-policy learning; useful negative phase diagrams are preserved; and the proposal explicitly withholds all present authority and all model, tokenizer, LoRA, GPU, locked-study, promotion, and claim authority. The paired RANDOM/MOTIF twins, constructive A2/A3/S targets, explicit graph and motif baselines, suffix noninterference, resource ledgers, and human-only promotion boundary could form a strong benchmark after exact repair. However, both independent interpretations correctly show that the present bytes leave outcome-determining choices to implementers and contain unresolved causal, visibility, scope, and comparator ambiguities. Therefore the exact six-atom CPU evidence-producing scope is not ratifiable as written. A successor reviewed change must hash-bind executable manifests and golden fixtures, resolve the RANDOM--MOTIF estimand, condition leakage and entropy on accepted-deck selection, close the capability and field-level visibility graph, limit AT06 to authorized CPU state, and bind the read-only PCFL-Stream comparator and decision table. A narrower authority to draft those successor proposal bytes could be considered, but it is not the canonical requested scope in these bytes. Later model/statistical concerns are nonblocking for that drafting-only step but remain mandatory gates. This critique, validation, consensus, or any later green CPU receipt grants no authority; only Rohin Ghosh may ratify exact successor bytes and exact scope.

concerns.statement: AMB_SYS_001 is sustained and blocks ratification of an executable CPU capability graph: E02, E03, and E06 name endpoints that are neither declared nodes nor explicitly owned subnodes.
concerns.evidence: The delta declares N01--N06 but uses DREAM, ChronologicalGrounding, SLEEPCompiler, and SealedScorerAudit as edge endpoints. Exact repair: a successor change must either declare these nodes or map each name to one declared owner, including runtime principal, reads, writes, and authority. Required test: MT02 must parse the graph, reject dangling endpoints, derive reachability, and prove that only L01-authorized CPU principals are reachable.

concerns.statement: AMB_SYS_002 is sustained: the CPU source/deck protocol and terminal sample are not derivable from the ratified bytes.
concerns.evidence: Era and episode counts, source schedule, target counts, budgets, accepted-versus-attempted stopping rule, and replacement policy alter public information, acceptance, yield, and resource results. Exact repair: bind a machine-readable schedule/deck manifest with all cardinalities, budgets, ordering, rejection, replacement, and stop rules before sampling. Required test: MT01 must reproduce golden manifests and identical terminal accepted/attempted counts across process and permitted platform reruns.

concerns.statement: AMB_SYS_003 is sustained: tau_q is outcome-determining but its domain and construction are unfrozen.
concerns.evidence: Different involutive derangements can cross raw/crafted types, preserve or break template automorphisms, and change feasibility or shortest paths. Exact repair: bind tau derivation, typed domain, automorphism constraints, site/candidate coupling, canonical ordering, and rejection behavior. Required test: MT03 must exhaustively prove involution, type preservation, recipe/binding equivariance, decisive-set mapping, equal public grammar, and equal path difficulty for golden and randomized quadruplets.

concerns.statement: AMB_SYS_004 is sustained: identified information and both MDL quantities lack executable definitions, so AT05 can change under equally plausible implementations.
concerns.evidence: No exact identification closure or complete prefix-free L_enum/L_schema codec is bound. Exact repair: freeze logical identification, encoder/decoder, template and model-class selection cost, permutations, bindings, deviations, exceptions, provenance, precision, rejected-model treatment, active-memory overhead, units, and matched-loss tolerance. Required test: MT04 must round-trip every code, prove prefix-freeness, match hand-computed golden bits, and show invariant information counts under serialization order.

concerns.evidence: Entry points, transitive imports, subprocesses, dynamic plugins, environment-controlled backends, filesystem roots, device APIs, credentials, and network resources are not closed. Exact repair before AT07: bind separate generative and recognition interfaces, output grammar, candidate visibility, hidden scans, lifetime dependence, tokens, latency, and byte/work budgets. concerns.statement: AMB_SYS_008 is sustained: AT06 is scope-ambiguous because literal compiler/memory hashes imply dormant N03/N04 implementation.

concerns.statement: BENCH_A007 is sustained: the CPU MDL report is not interpretable without complete prefix-free codecs and matched-loss tolerance.

concerns.statement: BENCH_A009 is sustained but is nonblocking for CPU construction; it is blocking before C2 because the slope alternative conflicts with the two-interval gate.

Required test: MT18 must reject synthetic data with a positive slope but either failed interval or failed retention.

concerns.statement: BENCH_A010 is sustained: AT05 requires MOTIF-only schema gain but never defines a fail-closed no-gain rule for RANDOM.

Exact repair: bind a simultaneous one-sided upper bound or equivalence interval, margin, family, unit, and failure disposition for full-schema minus atoms-only in RANDOM. Required test: MT12 must fail golden cases with a positive DiD but RANDOM gain outside the bound.

concerns.statement: BENCH_A011 is sustained: a constructive benchmark cannot hide impossible targets behind cohort-average .85 headroom.
concerns.evidence: A cohort oracle mean of .85 permits 15 percent impossible or misbudgeted targets and uneven failure by stratum; pooled .35 checks can similarly hide target leakage. Exact repair: require a per-target hidden-oracle path/solvability certificate, separately specified authentic-source-memory headroom, and predeclared tightly stratified aggregation for non-oracle thresholds. Required test: MT05 must reject every impossible target and cohorts whose leakage or headroom failure is masked by pooling.

concerns.statement: BENCH_A012 is sustained and nonblocking for absolute CPU cuts, but no CPU result may be called post-native and it is blocking before C2.
concerns.evidence: L_native depends on the future action model, tokenizer, prompt, serializers, workspace/history allowance, output reserve, truncation, and complete-event tie rule, all forbidden now. Exact repair before a model stage: hash-bind those exact bytes and derive cuts anew under separate authority; forbid relabeling CPU absolute cuts. Required test: MT19 must compute deterministic cuts from the bound model/tokenizer envelope and reject cut drift or retrospective relabeling.

concerns.statement: BENCH_A013 is sustained: unspecified probes cannot establish the AT04 leakage ceiling.

concerns.statement: BENCH_A014 is sustained but is nonblocking for CPU construction; it is blocking before causal organ attribution.

concerns.statement: BENCH_A015 is sustained and nonblocking for instrument construction if CPU resources are purely descriptive; it is blocking before comparative efficiency, scalability, or qualified C1 language.

concerns.statement: BENCH_A018 is sustained: the requested PCFL-Stream analytical comparison is not exact-byte scoped.

concerns.evidence: Generation, serialization, schedules, targets, controllers, semantic schemas, codecs, probes, statistics, and golden cases are absent or incomplete. concerns.statement: BENCH_D002 is accepted and nonblocking for world-only CPU work; one-atom and one-predicate claims are not credible before a bandwidth-bounded semantic grammar exists.

concerns.statement: BENCH_D003 is accepted and nonblocking for the CPU world; chronological evidence is necessary but not sufficient for broad DREAM proposal support.

concerns.statement: BENCH_D004 is accepted and nonblocking for negative-only CPU construction, but AT08 cannot authorize confirmation as written.

concerns.statement: BENCH_D006 is accepted: the current CPU instrument cannot certify MOTIF-only schema value or meaningful MDL behavior with the present gates.

concerns.statement: BENCH_D007 is accepted: cohort-average oracle headroom must not admit impossible constructive targets.
concerns.evidence: Impossible targets create guaranteed zeros and may be uneven by stratum; pooled leakage can also be hidden. concerns.statement: BENCH_D008 is accepted and exposes a central causal-design choice: shared RNG and schedules do not independently manipulate compressibility when binding-dependent outcomes alter a public-history-dependent collector.

concerns.statement: BENCH_D009 is accepted: hiding rejection receipts does not remove selection information from the benchmark distribution.

Required test: MT09 must inject acceptance-induced correlations and verify they are detected.

concerns.statement: BENCH_D010 is accepted and nonblocking for CPU construction: four-of-six, 70-percent-of-gold, below-five-percent, and point causal thresholds are engineering filters, not confirmatory organ evidence.
concerns.evidence: Denominators, uncertainty, data reuse, multiplicity, and model-state interventions are unfrozen, and CPU fixtures validate checkers rather than actual mediation. Required test: MT22 must lint artifacts and manuscripts so screen passage cannot satisfy a confirmatory claim gate.

concerns.statement: BENCH_D011 is accepted: cell reason strings cannot safely override coarse hidden/visible labels at implementation time.
concerns.evidence: Current targets versus split metadata, replay outcomes versus goals, atom content versus lifecycle metadata, roots versus workspace, and backend work versus returns need distinct types. Exact repair: bind field-level schemas, origin labels, declassification functions, process/storage ownership, and regenerate the full matrix. concerns.statement: BENCH_D012 is accepted: the analytical comparator and fallback decision can drift after FeltCraft results.
concerns.evidence: No PCFL-Stream path/hash or decision rubric is among the change's four contexts despite the comparison being one of six requested atoms. Exact repair: bind one read-only specification and a predeclared comparison table in the successor while preserving an absolute ban on PCFL implementation. Required test: MT14 must prove exact bytes, read-only access, stable criteria, and zero executable PCFL reachability.

concerns.statement: BENCH_D013 is accepted: the designer-supplied eight-role/four-recipe template cannot be free in any measured-compression result.
concerns.evidence: A privileged grammar makes L_schema shorter by construction and conflates oracle-code compressibility with learned DREAM compression. Exact repair: charge universal or preregistered model-class, decoder, template identification/selection, and alternative-model costs; report oracle-code and learned-code results separately and include alternative motif learners. concerns.statement: BENCH_D014 is accepted and nonblocking for CPU construction: behavioral change after a mask or twin substitution is insufficient for memory-mediated composition credit.
concerns.evidence: An intervention can be malformed, out of distribution, resource-changing, or incomplete over redundant paths; surviving behavior can use uncited memory. Exact repair before causal claims: fork the identical sealed state, change only registered semantic content with type/length/resource-matched controls, cut all redundant transitive paths, verify parser/retrieval invariants, and score twin-valid action changes separately from generic loss. Required test: MT20 must detect each exclusion and redundancy failure.

visibility_failures: E02, E03, and E06 use DREAM, ChronologicalGrounding, SLEEPCompiler, and SealedScorerAudit without declaring them as nodes or exact owned subprincipals, preventing closed reachability analysis.
I01 bundles replay outcomes with target goals, although DREAM may see the former and must not see the latter.
I03 bundles copied anchors, reader returns, cited roots, and workspace text, although grounding may audit roots but must not treat workspace or co-traversal as evidence.
I05 bundles the current public target with split, membership, score, and evaluation metadata, although THINK sees the target while reader/memory must not see the metadata.
I06 bundles semantic atom content with status, support counts, provenance, selector metadata, and compiler internals, although DREAM may see content but not the other fields.
I07 bundles backend-private candidate/search/training/resource work with the one-atom or NOT_FOUND return visible to cognition.
The AT06 suffix domain does not distinguish authorized CPU source/deck/controller state and inert canaries from forbidden future compiler, substrate, adapter, tokenizer, and model state.
One-atom and one-predicate channels lack semantic grammars and bit budgets, permitting target-bearing complete mappings or plans to cross nominally narrow interfaces.
missing_acceptance_tests: MT01_executable_manifest_and_golden_vectors: bind and replay the exact PRNG, tuple/key derivation, namespace strings, integer sampling, Unicode/serializer/version envelope, source schedule, target generator, cohort cardinalities, budgets, replacement and stopping rules across processes and permitted platforms.

MT02_graph_and_capability_referential_closure: reject dangling graph endpoints, bind every runtime principal and owner, derive the closed reachability graph, and prove that only authorized L01 CPU paths can execute.

MT03_tau_typed_equivariance: exhaustively verify the bound involutive derangement's typed domain, automorphism constraints, site/candidate coupling, round trip, decisive-set map, grammar identity, and path/difficulty equality.

MT04_identification_and_complete_codec: freeze edge-identification closure and prefix-free L_enum/L_schema encoders/decoders; round-trip golden cases; charge template/model selection, decoder, bindings, exceptions, provenance, precision, rejected models, and active memory at matched loss.

MT05_controller_cohort_and_solvability: bind each controller's information/interface/compute contract, require per-target hidden-oracle path certificates, distinguish legal-source exact memory from hidden oracle, and test stratified headroom/leakage plus boundary-valued aggregation.

MT06_closed_world_CPU_firewall: combine static dependency closure with denied-by-default process, environment, filesystem, credential, network, device, tokenizer/model, weight/adapter, locked-split, promotion, and PCFL-implementation enforcement before side effects.

MT07_field_level_visibility_and_taint: split bundled information items into typed fields with origins/declassification, regenerate the full stage product, and canary every forbidden field, storage path, cache, process, and downstream state.

MT08_scoped_CPU_suffix_noninterference: compare only authorized source/deck/controller/RNG/cache/report hashes plus inert canaries, deny real SLEEP/substrate/adapter/model code, and require a new full isolation audit under every later authorization.

MT09_acceptance_conditioned_entropy_and_Bayes: compute exact no-memory/source posteriors conditional on the full joint accepted-deck algorithm, report unconditional versus conditional quantities and all yields, and detect acceptance-induced target leakage.

MT10_S_target_identifiability_certificate: exhaustively enumerate legal-prefix and within-era evidence under accepted-deck conditioning and certify per-target MOTIF identification and RANDOM nonidentification without permutation-elimination leakage.

MT11_RANDOM_MOTIF_estimand_and_mediation: compare realized public histories, actions, exposures, identified relations, and information yield; enforce either a named total-effect-plus-mediation estimand or a predeclared matched-information controlled contrast.

MT12_CPU_schema_gain_and_verdict_table: bind the minimum MOTIF gain, simultaneous RANDOM no-gain/equivalence rule, MDL reporting-versus-threshold decision, exact denominators, and retain/rework/reject outcomes; exercise all boundary cases.
